answer: With a Registered domain bound by DNS record proof with revocation on transfer, the account is only as strong as its binding: the registered domain answers a fresh challenge, the DNS record proof is recorded, and revocation on transfer keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so losing the channel means losing the identity, and fakes cannot hide behind throwaway channels. The record keeps every grove visible, so anyone can audit the binding roll. Between a pearl and a dawn lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to bind.
